title: Program Analyst  (Data Analyst)
job_summary: This position is located in the Bureau of African Affairs (AF) Executive office (EX) Remote Support Division (RSD) Department of State (DOS).
duties_text: Conducts complex data analysis to evaluate program effectiveness, inform policy decisions, and assess the impact of legislation or regulations. Oversees contract and project performance by monitoring progress, evaluating contractor achievement of goals, and assessing risk to ensure effective operations and compliance with regulations. Provides technical guidance on data analysis and automation opportunities to enhance program efficiency, including evaluating processes and recommending improvements.
qualifications_text: Applicants must meet all the required qualification requirements described below by the closing date of this announcement. NOTE: Applicants must meet time-in-grade and time after competitive appointment requirements, by the closing date of this announcement. Time-In-Grade Requirements: Federal applicants must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade to satisfy time-in-grade restrictions, per 5CFR 300, Subpart F. Applicants must have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 level in the Federal service which provided the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the duties of the position. Qualifying specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience in translating complex data analytics concepts into clear, concise reports and evaluating program effectiveness. Analyzing and evaluating Bureau or Department functions related to data analyst projects. Experience utilizing software/or programs to conduct data analysis. There is no substitute of education for specialized experience for the GS-14 position.

Applicants who meet the minimum qualification requirements, as described in the “Qualifications” section of this announcement, will be assigned a score between 70 and 100. The evaluation process consists of an online assessment and a subject matter expert resume review of applicants found to be among the top qualified candidates based on the crediting plan assessment. Resumes longer than two pages will be deemed ineligible and will not be considered further. Responses to questions that are not fully supported by the information in your resume may result in adjustments to your rating. Your qualifications will be evaluated on the following competencies: . Knowledge and experience applying quantitative and qualitative methods Knowledge of records management and archive control theories. Applicants found to be among the top qualified candidates will be referred to the hiring official for further consideration and possible interview. Qualified non-competitive candidates must be deemed best qualified based on the applicant assessment in order to be referred to the hiring official for further consideration and possible interview. Your resume should demonstrate how you meet all aspects of the specialized experience statement. SMEs will not review additional information beyond your resume (e.g., links embedded in your resume will not be opened.). If meeting basic qualifications through education only or a combination of education and experience, applicants will not be referred to the SME panel but will be reviewed by the HR Specialist for referral. Agency Career and Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP and ICTAP) candidates must be considered well-qualified for the position and submit the supporting documents listed under the required documents section of this job announcement to receive consideration for selection priority. To be considered well-qualified, in addition to earning a score of 85 or above and meeting minimum qualifications, candidates must demonstrate proficiency in some, but not all of the major aspects of the position. title: Data Analyst
job_summary: This position is located at the Dayton VA Medical Center (VAMC) organizationally aligned under Community and Public Relations and the Veteran Experience Office (VEO) and will collect, analyze and validate various data concerning patient experience to include, but not limited to, Survey of Healthcare Experience of Patients (SHEP), Veteran Signals (V-Signals) and Patient Advocate Tracking System Replacement (PATS-R) etc. 2 Page Resume Limit DOES APPLY for this position
duties_text: Duties include: Prepares and analyzes reports for service lines related to Veteran satisfaction issues for the respective services. Analyzes trends, proposes process improvement and ensures capturing and communicating data analysis and trends to various Councils, Committees and Service meetings. Presents executive leadership, service leaders and management with detailed reports, findings and recommendations in regards to data quality and process improvements and initiatives to improve veteran experience and satisfaction. Makes significant contributions and/or provides technical leadership to high visibility projects to assist in identifying and resolving issues of strategic importance to the organization. Report Generation and Distribution: Prepare, validate, and distribute regular and ad hoc reports summarizing findings and recommendations for executive leadership, service chiefs, and program managers. Analyze data to identify trends, performance benchmarks, and improvement opportunities related to Veteran satisfaction. Conduct in-depth research and complex analyses on patient experience issues; provide expert recommendations and support special projects related to organizational improvement. Collaborates with all members of the health care team, Medical Center Administration, Site Managers' Offices and Executive Leadership. Participate in committees, councils, process improvement teams, and other forums as required to report on data findings and support strategic planning. Present findings and recommendations clearly in both written and oral formats; interact with stakeholders in a professional, respectful, and effective manner. Work Schedule: Full-Time, Monday-Friday, 7:30am - 4:00pm. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Position Description/PD#: Data Analyst/PD92028A Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized. Critical Skills Incentive (CSI): Not Approved. Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized.
qualifications_text: To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 09/29/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement. For a GS-11 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-09. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials. If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade. Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment. You may qualify based on your experience and/or education as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-09 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization. Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Interpreting pertinent laws, policies, and regulations, applicable to business initiatives, program goals, and objectives, and using analytical methods to assess and recommend improvements for program effectiveness and management processes and systems to maintain administrative operations. OR, Education: Applicants may substitute education for the required experience. To qualify based on education for this grade level you must have a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or LL.M., (if related) or I have completed three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree and which demonstrates the competencies necessary to do the work. OR, Combination: Applicants may also combine education and experience to qualify at this level. You must have an combination of specialized experience and education beyond masters degree. [Note: To combine education and experience, first determine how much of the qualifying experience and education you have, as a percentage of what is required for each. Add the percentages together, and if the total is 100% or more, then the combined education and experience is qualifying for the position. EXAMPLE: To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of education beyond the first 18 semester hours (i.e. beyond the first year) by 18. Add the two percentages together. The total percentage must equal at least 100% to qualify.]. Physical Demands: No special physical demands such as above average ability, dexterity, or strength are required to perform the work. Work is sedentary and the employee may sit comfortably. May be subject to stressful situations due to short turnaround timeframes required by requests from offices within Dayton VAMC, including Offices of the Director and Associate Director. As such, this position demands emotional stability. There may be some walking, standing, bending, carrying of light items, driving of an automobile, etc. For more information on these qualification standards, please visit the United States Office of Personnel Management's website at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/.
requirements_text: You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job. To be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process. In addition to the application and questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job. Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959. Subject to background/security investigation. Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued identification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment. Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP). As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period or 2-year trial period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

title: Program Analyst (Data Analyst)
job_summary: Organizational Location: This position is with the Department of Homeland Security, within U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Accountability, Performance Management and Analysis Division, located in Washington, DC. Additional selections may be made to include other organizational divisions and/or units within the duty location(s) listed above.
duties_text: Joining Customs & Border Protection (CBP), Office of Accountability, will allow you to utilize your expertise to serve as an advance Program Analyst responsible for providing analytics expertise to programs and offices across CBP. This position starts at a salary of $102,415.00 (GS-12, Step 1) to $158,322.00 (GS-13, Step 10). Apply for this exciting opportunity to strengthen the Department's ability to perform homeland security functions by serving as an expert analyst on current analytical tools and techniques, advisor to CBP organizational elements on applying analytics to their challenges, as a reviewer thereof, and data expert to improve analytics with CBP Enterprise Services, as well as CBP Policy, resource, and operational problems and projects. GS Salary: Visit this link to view the locality pay tables by geographic area. If you do not see your geographic area listed, select the "Rest of United States" pay table. Some positions fall under a special pay rate depending on the series, grade level and location of the position. Please visit this link to view special pay rate charts. In this Program Analyst position you will become a key team member of Homeland Security professionals involved in leading, planning, developing, monitoring, coordinating, and implementing data analysis and data analytics projects to resolve critical operational, policy, and resourcing issues; analyzing agency administrative aspects of substantive, mission-orientated programs; and recommending and applying new hypotheses and concepts to improve effectiveness and efficiency of operations to resolve policy questions Typical Work assignments include: Applying expert data management and analysis techniques to study, gather, interpret, develop, and report on CBP operational, policy, and performance data. Developing and preparing s a variety of dashboards, analytical reports, memoranda, and technical documents to assist ongoing monitoring, inspections, and assessment to improve Agency performance. Planning, researching, and implementing the full scope of data analytical projects requiring interpretation, inspection, research, and application of performance management data. Providing expertise and guidance to staff and leadership on questions related to analysis and analytic methods involving performing quantitative and qualitative analysis, data quality assurance, developing graphics and reports based on the analysis and interpretation of data, and delivers analytical capabilities to operational offices. Serving as project manager or office representative on multi-office teams and leading coordination of group efforts for cross-component analytics projects; developing and reviewing analytics pilot project plans and identifying areas of improvement in CBP self-service analytics capabilities and performance.
qualifications_text: Specialized Experience: GS-12: You qualify for the GS-12 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Evaluating operational or performance data to identify trends, data quality issues, or program impacts. Developing dashboards, reports, graphics, or data visualizations to support program monitoring and decision-making. Conducting qualitative or quantitative analyses to assess program effectiveness, efficiency, or performance. Preparing written reports, memoranda, graphics, or technical documentation that communicate analytical results, data limitations, issues identified, and recommended improvements. GS-13: You qualify for the GS-13 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Leading data analytics projects to assess program performance or operational effectiveness. Developing analytical methods, dashboards, or reports to improve performance monitoring. Advising management on analytical findings, data quality issues, or corrective actions. Coordinating cross-office analytics efforts to resolve data issues or improve processes. NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible. Please see the "Required Documents" section below for additional resume requirements. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You must: Meet all qualification requirements, including education if applicable to this position, subject to verification at any stage of the application process; and Meet all applicable Time in Grade requirements (current federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade or equivalent grade band in the federal service) by 09/29/2026. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Background Investigation: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity. During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances. job_summary: This position is located in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Office of Strategy, Policy and Plans (PLCY), Office of Homeland Security Statistics (OHSS). duties_text: As a Program Analyst (Data Analytics), GS-0343-13, your typical work assignments may include: Serving as a data analyst to support DHS data related solutions for privacy compliance, disclosure avoidance, and applying a variety of analytical approaches to solve mission focused policy, methodologies, and/or administrative problems in a fast -paced environment. Leading and integrating data lifecycle management activities and data quality measures; improving the collection of data from varying sources, formats, and quality and preparing them for analysis and dissemination. Serving as a data governance lead to support technical data lifecycle processes, including applying programming, statistical, business intelligence, or data management tools to advance enterprise data governance objectives; including evaluating large datasets for quality, consistency, completeness, lineage, and usability; supporting data standards and metadata practices; and communicating governance insights through dashboards, reports, or other decision-support products. Presenting the findings of subject matter experts and analytical products to policymakers and non-technical audience. This announcement will be open for 5 business days OR until the first 100 applications have been received, whichever happens first. Exercising project management and IT systems development with Agile methodology; leading and integrating data lifecycle management activities and data quality measures; improving the collection of data from varying sources, formats, and quality and preparing them for analysis and dissemination. title: Human Capital Data Analyst
job_summary: This position is within Internal Operations (HSI), Technology & Internal Operations (HS), Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) Human Resources Service Center (H), Office of the Chief Human Capital Officer (HC), Department of Energy (DOE). Drive strategic impact as a senior workforce analytics expert! Turn complex personnel data into interactive dashboards and actionable insights that guide executive leaders to solve high-stakes staffing challenges and shape the future of our workforce.
duties_text: Powering the Pacific Northwest Through Data: Shape the Future of Our Workforce! Join an Impact-Driven Team At Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), we deliver clean, reliable, and sustainable energy to millions of people across the Pacific Northwest. Our mission succeeds because of our people-and that is where you come in. As a Human Capital Data Analyst, you won't just analyze data; you will be the strategic engine behind our talent strategy. You will turn complex workforce metrics into executive insights, design modern digital tools, and guide senior leaders through high-stakes organizational decisions. If you are a collaborative problem-solver who loves transforming raw information into actionable strategies, this is your opportunity to build a rewarding career with immense public impact. Key Duties & Responsibilities 1. Design Interactive Data Dashboards and Tools: Build, maintain, and modernize user-friendly visual reports, tracking systems, and digital dashboards. You will turn raw workforce numbers into visual stories that help leadership easily monitor organizational health and make key staffing decisions. 2. Lead Cross-Agency Data Collaborations: Partner with diverse departments across BPA and the wider Department of Energy to gather, organize, and synthesize large, complex data sets. You will build collaborative pathways to access the essential statistics needed to plan our future workforce. 3. Guide Strategic Executive Decision-Making: Deliver clear, evidence-based recommendations and alternative solutions to executive-level agency leaders. You will evaluate the potential pros, cons, and structural impacts of workforce changes, helping leaders make confident, informed choices. 4. Serve as a Trusted Strategic HR Advisor: Provide expert counsel to executives, managers, and senior staff on organizational structure, staffing strategies, and human capital regulations. You will translate complex policy language into clear, practical, and everyday business advice. 5. Shape the Long-Term Workforce Strategy: Evaluate, refine, and drive long-range workforce plans, talent management strategies, and major organizational studies. Your analysis will ensure our agency maintains the right talent in the right positions to fulfill our energy mission. 6. Modernize HR Metrics and Data Integrity: Develop clear guidelines and processes to define, clean, merge, and transform workforce data. By setting high standards for data quality, you will ensure our predictive models and analysis are accurate, trustworthy, and actionable. 7. Translate Technical Insights for General Audiences: Simplify complex statistical findings, database trends, and technical methodologies into highly engaging, easy-to-understand presentations and educational materials for non-technical managers and staff. 8. Drive High-Impact Projects Autonomously: Take independent ownership of workforce analysis projects from start to finish. You will manage milestones, coordinate with cross-functional project teams, navigate shifting priorities, and deliver high-quality, practical solutions on time.
qualifications_text: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-12) in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as: experience 1) extracting, synthesizing, and analyzing complex workforce data using analytics and visualization tools to build metrics, reports, and interactive dashboards; 2) conducting workforce planning studies and evaluating organizational staffing trends to develop actionable recommendations for complex resourcing issues; and 3) providing analytical advisory services, technical briefings, or strategic guidance to leadership on workforce management practices and operational alignment. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. job_summary: This position serves as a Data Analyst in the National Center for Warrior Independence (NCWI) at the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. This position will use large databases and complex multi-site, multi-source datasets to create reports, tools, and dashboards to directly support the decision-making and reporting needs of NCWI leadership and staff.
duties_text: Total Rewards VA Benefits Key job duties include, but are not limited to the following: Incumbent serves as an authoritative technical expert and consultant to NCWI group leaders on data management, data mining, and data representation techniques that inform the monitoring, evaluation, and improvement of programs. Advise and participate in the development of health informatics systems that can be used to appropriately monitor clinical care processes, outcomes, and patient safety. Design, develop and support the technology infrastructure for the extraction, report interface, creation, storage, and seamless presentation of clinical and administrative data available throughout VHA. Design, implement, and maintain database applications, dashboards, data reporting systems, data sets, and databases that synthesize clinical and administrative data from multiple sources into meaningful and useful information and knowledge for business analysis purposes. Will work with the NCWI Clinical Informatics team to create a repository of reports and tools. Data sources for decision support tools will include VistA, CDW, EDIS, MCA, ARC, FMS, PAID, and other data sources. Performs regular analytical reviews of facility data. Identifies operational, clinical, and financial scenarios for analysis and recommends ways to optimize efficiency, cost management, resource utilization, and risk reduction. Develops logic and writes code to extract data from CDW, VistA and other local or national databases. Identify trends and analyzes homeless program data. Provides statistical analyses in support of current metrics and development of new performance/operational measures. Participates in defining strategic goals, developing, and implementing administrative and clinic programs, and educating staff regarding processes related to data management, research, assisting in measurement of those goals, and contributing to the success of those projects. Demonstrates skill in effective written and oral communication, to include expertise in data visualization and expert knowledge of a broad range of computer-based programs for communication, report generation, and presentations. Compiles final reports, including comprehensive analyses. Other duties as assigned. Work Schedule: Various tours of duty based on the needs of the service. Compressed/Flexible: May be available based on the needs of the service. job_summary: This position serves as a Supervisory Data Analyst in the National Center for Warrior Independence (NCWI) at the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. duties_text: Total Rewards VA Benefits Key job duties include, but are not limited to the following: Incumbent oversees the daily operation of the unit, ensures that agency policies and priorities are being followed; develops performance standards; and evaluates work performance of all subordinates assigned. job_summary: The Management and Program Analyst (Systems Redesign/Data Analytics) is assigned to the High Reliability, Patient Safety & Process Improvement Section within the Quality Safety & Value (QSV) Service. The organization provides Medical, Surgical, Psychiatric, Rehabilitative, Geriatric care in a variety of acute, outpatient, and residential settings.
duties_text: Duties include, but may not be limited to the following: Data Analytics and Performance Measurement The incumbent serves as the facility's principal analyst for hospital performance measures and metrics, including SAIL, Hospital Compare, VSSC indicators, and related national/VISN-reported data, which are used to assess and compare medical center performance. The incumbent independently retrieves, tracks, and trends data from the Corporate Data Warehouse, VSSC, Pyramid Analytics, VistA, and other systems, identifying facility-wide performance risks and opportunities proactively, before they are flagged externally by VISN or VACO. The incumbent analyzes data to make quantitative and qualitative evaluations, identifying trends and discrepancies related to performance metrics, and prepares narrative and statistical reports of findings for review by QSV leadership, service chiefs, committees, and executive leadership. The incumbent employs management analysis techniques and methods to develop and refine information for comprehensive reports addressing cost analysis, work measurement, trend analysis, efficiency, effectiveness, productivity, and tangible benefits, and to assess the success or failure in attaining program operational goals and objectives. The incumbent develops, maintains, and continuously improves dashboards, scorecards, and data visualization tools to communicate performance status and trends clearly to a variety of clinical and administrative audiences. The incumbent identifies data quality issues, investigates root causes, and works directly with responsible services or data stewards across organizational lines to resolve discrepancies and ensure data integrity. The incumbent coordinates ongoing data collection efforts across services and programs, ensuring timely submission of data and monitoring completion of data-related deliverables, and ensures the facility is current on all performance measure targets identified by the VAMC, VISN, and VA Central Office (VACO) leadership. The incumbent prepares complete and fully documented analytical projects and reports for review by VAMC committees and/or Executive Leadership, and presents findings and recommendations in briefings to managers and leaders using formats appropriate for both clinical and administrative audiences. The incumbent assists in participation in Root Cause Analyses, proactive Risk Assessments, and Quality Tracers by providing relevant data analysis to support findings and corrective action planning, and uses statistical process control and other Total Quality Management (TQM) tools to evaluate current processes and support evidence-based decision-making. Systems Redesign / Process Improvement The incumbent provides analytical and facilitation support for process improvement activities across the VAMC, using data findings to identify and refer improvement initiatives to appropriate subject matter experts. The incumbent independently identifies, plans, and executes system redesign initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and other process improvement methodologies, in direct response to data trend findings. The incumbent leads or co-facilitates process improvement workshops and flow mapping exercises tied to data-identified performance gaps, working proactively across service lines. The incumbent develops training materials, standard operating procedures, and workflow standardization efforts, particularly where data indicates facility-wide (rather than isolated) performance concerns. The incumbent facilitates and promotes the development of a true High Reliability Organization culture across every aspect of the hospital, and supports HRO principles in every phase of process improvement work. Promotion Potential: The full performance level is the GS-12. Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 7:00AM -3:30PM Telework: Not Authorized Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Solves problems/issues quickly and effectively, involving a methodical step-by-step approach to thinking; breaks down complex problems into single and manageable components and considers each part in detail; makes a systematic comparison of various alternatives; notices discrepancies and inconsistencies in available information; identifies a set of features, parameters, or considerations to take into account. Specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Qualifying specialized experience includes knowledge of a wide range of qualitative and quantitative methods for analyzing and measuring the effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity of administrative, clinical, and technical programs, along with knowledge of the mission, organization, and work processes of programs throughout the VAMC, and knowledge of health care systems and delivery systems. An understanding of performance improvement principles, including general systems theory, Lean Thinking, and Six Sigma, and the analytical techniques required to support QSV leadership and the Executive Leadership Team in planning, organizing, and implementing Performance Improvement and High Reliability initiatives. The full performance level of this position is GS12; candidate may be selected at the GS11 or GS12 grade level only. Promotion Potential: The GS-12 is the Full Performance Level. Experience should include independently retrieving and analyzing data from VA systems such as the Corporate Data Warehouse (CDW), VSSC, Pyramid Analytics, or VistA; developing dashboards, scorecards, or data visualizations (e.g., using Power BI); and preparing narrative and statistical reports for senior leadership and committees. Experience applying Lean, Six Sigma, or other process/systems redesign methodologies to facilitate performance improvement initiatives in a healthcare setting is highly desired. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religions; spiritual; community; student; social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Physical Requirements: The work is generally sedentary; however, there will be some walking, standing, bending, and carrying of light items such as papers and books. The tasks may require long periods at a desk working on a personal computer or other piece of equipment. The work also involves coping with complex, persistent demands from a variety of sources that can be regarded as a high-pressure work situation. The analyst will be required to visit all areas of the medical center both on campus and report sites such as CBOCs or leased spaces. Contact with medical center employees, supervisors and top management in all areas of the facility is required. Duties include, but may not be limited to the following: Data Analytics and Performance Measurement The incumbent serves as the facility's principal analyst for hospital performance measures and metrics, including SAIL, Hospital Compare, VSSC indicators, and related national/VISN-reported data, which are used to assess and compare medical center performance. The incumbent independently retrieves, tracks, and trends data from the Corporate Data Warehouse, VSSC, Pyramid Analytics, VistA, and other systems, identifying facility-wide performance risks and opportunities proactively, before they are flagged externally by VISN or VACO. The incumbent analyzes data to make quantitative and qualitative evaluations, identifying trends and discrepancies related to performance metrics, and prepares narrative and statistical reports of findings for review by QSV leadership, service chiefs, committees, and executive leadership. The incumbent employs management analysis techniques and methods to develop and refine information for comprehensive reports addressing cost analysis, work measurement, trend analysis, efficiency, effectiveness, productivity, and tangible benefits, and to assess the success or failure in attaining program operational goals and objectives. The incumbent develops, maintains, and continuously improves dashboards, scorecards, and data visualization tools to communicate performance status and trends clearly to a variety of clinical and administrative audiences. The incumbent identifies data quality issues, investigates root causes, and works directly with responsible services or data stewards across organizational lines to resolve discrepancies and ensure data integrity. The incumbent coordinates ongoing data collection efforts across services and programs, ensuring timely submission of data and monitoring completion of data-related deliverables, and ensures the facility is current on all performance measure targets identified by the VAMC, VISN, and VA Central Office (VACO) leadership. The incumbent prepares complete and fully documented analytical projects and reports for review by VAMC committees and/or Executive Leadership, and presents findings and recommendations in briefings to managers and leaders using formats appropriate for both clinical and administrative audiences. The incumbent assists in participation in Root Cause Analyses, proactive Risk Assessments, and Quality Tracers by providing relevant data analysis to support findings and corrective action planning, and uses statistical process control and other Total Quality Management (TQM) tools to evaluate current processes and support evidence-based decision-making. Systems Redesign / Process Improvement The incumbent provides analytical and facilitation support for process improvement activities across the VAMC, using data findings to identify and refer improvement initiatives to appropriate subject matter experts. The incumbent independently identifies, plans, and executes system redesign initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and other process improvement methodologies, in direct response to data trend findings. The incumbent leads or co-facilitates process improvement workshops and flow mapping exercises tied to data-identified performance gaps, working proactively across service lines. The incumbent develops training materials, standard operating procedures, and workflow standardization efforts, particularly where data indicates facility-wide (rather than isolated) performance concerns. The incumbent facilitates and promotes the development of a true High Reliability Organization culture across every aspect of the hospital, and supports HRO principles in every phase of process improvement work. Promotion Potential: The full performance level is the GS-12. Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 7:00AM -3:30PM Telework: Not Authorized Virtual: This is not a virtual position. job_summary: You will serve as a OPERATIONS RESEARCH ANALYST in the DATA ANALYTICS DIRECTORATE of NAVSAFECOM.
duties_text: You will coordinate the development and management of data science and artificial intelligence/machine learning projects, including objectives, project plans, schedules, and support requirements. You will translate naval safety questions and operational needs into analytical studies, determine data collection requirements, select and adapt methodologies, organize project phases, and derive conclusions and recommendations. You will design and implement relational or dimensional data models and repeatable data pipelines to extract, integrate, clean, transform, and validate data for analysis. You will develop, test, and document reusable analytical code using tools such as Python and SQL in environments such as Databricks. You will evaluate and coordinate requests for data science and machine learning analysis, advise stakeholders on feasibility, and adapt analytical approaches or propose alternative data sources to address data limitations and time constraints. You will develop reports of analytical findings and model conclusions, including charts, tables, dashboards, and presentations. You will provide recommendations that help technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior leaders, make informed safety and risk decisions You will initiate and conduct complex research on safety-related topics, including those with limited precedent, and develop, train, and validate machine learning models for prediction, classification, and risk analysis. You will use statistical analysis and appropriate evaluation methods to assess model performance, assumptions, uncertainty, and limitations.
qualifications_text: In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-12) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a professional Operations Research Analyst performing the following duties: 1. Advanced Modeling - Experience independently developing, validating, and applying machine learning models for prediction, anomaly detection, or risk analysis, including evaluating model performance, assumptions, and limitations. 2. Programming & Pipelines - Professional experience performing hands-on data engineering and exploratory data analysis using languages such as Python and SQL including building ETL/data pipelines to ingest, integrate, clean, validate, and transform data for analysis and machine learning. 3. Experience leading or substantially contributing to data science project lifecycles, including defining analytical objectives, identifying data requirements, coordinating data integration, addressing data quality, and documenting analytical methods, model validation results, and recommendations. 4. Experience designing interactive dashboards (e.g., Qlik, Tableau, PowerBI) and presenting highly technical model outputs, limitations, and predictive insights to Flag-level leadership. job_summary: You will serve as a GG-13 senior Acoustic Intelligence (ACINT) Analyst responsible for analyzing, evaluating, and interpreting raw ACINT data. You will use analytical techniques in Sound Pressure Level (SPL) measurements, acoustic signal processing theory, and sensor certification to complete assignments. This position is located within the ACINT Department of FARRAGUT TECHNICAL ANALYSIS CENTER in Suitland, Maryland.
duties_text: You will exploit acoustic data using specialized signal processing and analysis equipment and software installed in the National Acoustic Intelligence (ACINT) Laboratory. You will employ Target Motion Analysis (TMA) techniques and analytical techniques used in Sound Pressure Level (SPL) measurements, acoustic signal processing theory, and sensor certification. You will apply Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR) gram analysis and beamforming techniques to daily Acoustic Intelligence (ACINT) analysis. You will develop, tailor, prepare, and communicate detailed technical and intelligence-based acoustic assessments and other products that represent the command position of foreign naval threat platforms acoustic signatures. You will draw on board expertise to effectively interact and coordinate with senior Intelligence Community (IC) members and foreign counterparts.

Oversees the human capital data and methodologies employed to capture, utilize and disseminate that data. Leads enterprise-wide workforce planning initiatives and performs advanced human capital data analysis to forecast workforce objectives in andinform strategic alignment. Evaluates and makes authoritative recommendations for the best approaches, methodologies, and instruments for collecting human capital and workforce data. Provides expert advisory and consultative services to all levels of management on issues affecting the full range of workforce planning, recruitment, and human capital initiatives. Develops human capital goals, measures, metrics, and targets for strategic plans. The ideal candidate will possess the skill to analyze large, complex data sets to derive human capital insights. Extracting data from automated HR databases to identify systemic organizational trends and forecast long-term workforce objectives for senior leadership decision-making. He/She will possess effective communication skills to meet the customer at their level with the ability to translate intricate workforce metrics and legislative guidance into tailored briefings and actionable reports. He/She will enable diverse stakeholders and senior agency officials to easily comprehend and execute strategic initiatives. And, he/she will possess critical thinking & proactive inquiry to drive the best work product. Investigating ambiguous, poorly defined workforce challenges through independent research and targeted stakeholder inquiries to formulate innovative methodologies and deliver high-quality strategic work products where guidelines are scarce.

Experience investigating workforce planning challenges through proactive inquiry to deliver strategic products where definitive operational guidelines may be limited. job_summary: This position is located with Bonneville Power Administration in Process, Data and Information Systems (TIBP), Internal Operations (TIB), Transmission Infrastructure Asset Management (TI), Transmission Services (T), Bonneville Power Administration (BPA). A successful candidate in the Business Analyst position will serve as a Business Analyst to evaluate Transmission Field Services/Infrastructure Asset Management project business proposals, plan and oversee project execution.
duties_text: As a Business Analyst, you will: Lead High-Impact, Cross-Functional Initiatives Head collaborative teams of multi-disciplinary experts to evaluate, shape, and execute complex business and infrastructure proposals. You will serve as the driving force behind projects from early-stage concepts to successful, long-term implementation. Drive Prosci-Aligned Change Management Design and execute comprehensive organizational change strategies utilizing the industry-standard Prosci methodology. You will build and implement tailored plans for training, communication, and coaching to minimize disruption and ensure team buy-in across departmental lines. Design and Reengineer Business Processes Serve as a trusted advisor in analyzing workflows, identifying operational bottlenecks, and designing modern, technology-enabled processes. Your work will directly enhance organizational efficiency, resource utilization, and decision-making capabilities. Perform Advanced Risk and Financial Analysis Conduct deep-dive risk assessments and financial evaluations to predict project outcomes, optimize resource allocation, and implement project controls. You will provide critical insights to ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and on budget. Direct End-to-End Project and Portfolio Execution Take ownership of project milestones, schedules, and deliverables. You will seamlessly integrate active initiatives into the broader organizational portfolio and develop performance metrics to track and evaluate success over time. Coach and Advise Leadership at All Levels Provide expert guidance and coaching to managers and senior executives to build strong leadership sponsorship for strategic transitions. You will empower leaders to effectively guide their teams through complex organizational shifts. Integrate Cutting-Edge Technology Solutions Collaborate with technology teams to identify, adopt, and integrate modern software applications and systems. You will ensure that digital tools are seamlessly incorporated into daily workflows to support grid operations and physical infrastructure projects. Champion Stakeholder Engagement and Influence Build consensus, resolve conflicts, and cultivate collaborative relationships across the agency and with external partners. You will present compelling, data-driven findings to executives, persuading decision-makers to adopt solutions that align with the region's energy strategy.

duties_text: Some of the major duties you will perform include but are not limited to the following: Administer and Manage ArcGIS Online. Works with customers, stakeholders, subject matter experts, and specialists across the Service to define requirements and develop geospatial and data management processes/workflows/tools to support the Mission of the Bureau. Supports enterprise geospatial operations through automation of tasks within web, cloud, and desktop-based environments, including customization using FME and Microsoft tools such as SharePoint and the Power Platform. Collaborates with system architects, business users, project managers, and other developers, and the full geospatial community to achieve desirable solutions for new geospatial tools. title: Supervisory Program Analyst
job_summary: This position is part of DHRA. The incumbent of this position serves as the Supervisory Program Analyst, Resource Management Division, and Defense Manpower Data Center. The Financial Management Division is responsible for accomplishing a wide variety of financial and analytical duties in the planning, analyzing, formulating, justifying, presenting, executing, and reviewing the financial budgets for Operations and Maintenance, Procurement Defense Agencies, and Research and Development.
duties_text: As a Supervisory Program Analyst at the GS-0343-14 level some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as a subject matter expert in federal finance, leading the organization's participation in the DoD's Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process. Formulates, justifies, and executes the financial budgets for multiple appropriations, including Operations and Maintenance (O&M), Procurement, and Research, Development, Testing, and Evaluation (RDT&E). Provides expert advice and technical assistance on budgets, workload, and resource management to senior leadership, including the Director and Program and Division Leaders. Identifies and analyzes potential funding problems, calculates risks, and develops recommendations for management to resolve budgetary issues, such as reprogramming funds or adjusting execution plans. Monitors the execution of the approved operating budget to ensure funds are properly allocated and spent in a timely manner, and establishes financial procedures to prevent violations. Reviews and analyzes financial reports and data from various parts of the organization to establish the annual budget estimate, ensure compliance with policy, and support long-term program requirements. Performs supervisory duties, including planning and coordinating the work of team members, developing performance plans, providing technical and administrative guidance, and handling personnel actions.
qualifications_text: You may qualify at the GS-14, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Performing financial and program analysis for an organization. Participating in the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process. Preparing and justifying financial budgets for operations, procurement, or research and development. Providing advice on resource management and budgetary matters. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. *Preference will be given to applicants who possess Financial Management Certification.

title: Program Analyst
job_summary: The employee will serve as the Program Analyst, located int the Data & Information Department, Veterans Crisis Line (VCL), Veterans Affairs (VA). The VCL is a 24-hour, 7-days-a-week, 365-days-a-year service aimed at connecting callers worldwide to a caring, qualified VA employee. The VCL's mission is to provide 24/7, world-class suicide prevention and crisis intervention services to Veterans, Service Members, and their family members.
duties_text: Major duties include but are not limited to: Helping to manage documents and historical records to maintain data accuracy and integrity of databases, spreadsheets, tables, and data warehouse. Identifying irregularities in statistical trends or in statistical data. Evaluating, selecting, and modifying statistical methodologies and techniques to determine the most appropriate procedures for efficiency, reliability, and feasibility in call center operations. Coordinating the determination of the scope of surveys, optimum sample sizes, appropriate sampling procedures, and quantification of the reliability of estimates based on samples. Performs other duties as assigned by management. Work Schedule: Tour of Duty is typically Administrative Hours. Flexible Schedule may be available after training. VCL has multiple tours that cover our 24/7/365 operations (this does include Holidays). Tour is subject to change based on program needs. Remote: Yes, this is a remote position. Selectees will work 100% of the time in a non-VA-owned space outside of the local commuting area of a parent station. The employee's workspace must be suitable for conducting business and as such, remote employees are expected to provide a secure, distraction-free home-based worksite with reliable high speed internet connectivity. The employee will be required to travel to the closest VA Medical Center or VA Outpatient Clinic for issuance of equipment, and as needed for technical support. Selectees will be required to self-certify that their remote workplace meets all safety, privacy, and internet speed requirements. Position Description/PD#: Program Analyst/PD07630A Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized Financial Disclosure Report: Not required

title: Nurse-Clinical Analyst
job_summary: Nurse (Clinical Analyst) demonstrates leadership, advanced analytical expertise, and systems thinking in support of organizational quality, patient safety, accreditation readiness, and performance improvement initiatives throughout the medical center. The incumbent applies knowledge of healthcare data, clinical processes, organizational performance, information systems, quality management principles, and evidence-based practice to improve clinical and operational outcomes.
duties_text: Located in the Rogue Valley, White City allows easy access to Metro-area of Medford while remaining engrossed with nature. White City is an unincorporated community in Jackson County, Oregon, in the Rogue Valley. It is about nine miles north of Medford and 34 miles north of the California border. Enjoy the scenic drives to either Crater Lake, Oregon's only National Park, and to the mountain resort Lake of the Woods. Take a family-friendly hike to a waterfall or ride the only section of the Pacific Crest Trail that's open to mountain bikers. Nurse (Clinical Analyst) provides facility-level leadership in the development, governance, validation, interpretation, and analysis of clinical and operational data to support nursing evaluation, healthcare quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and organizational performance improvement. Duties include but not limited to: Leads and facilitates Lean improvement projects, Rapid Process Improvement Workshops (RPIWs), process mapping, workflow redesign, and performance improvement initiatives across clinical and administrative services. Applies Lean, Systems Redesign, Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA), root cause analysis, change management, and evidence-based improvement methodologies to improve quality, patient safety, efficiency, access, and the Veteran experience. Provides consultation, facilitation, and coaching to executive leadership, managers, supervisors, and frontline staff regarding organizational improvement strategies. Develops project charters, implementation plans, outcome measures, sustainability plans, and executive reports for improvement initiatives. Monitors project outcomes through performance metrics and data analysis to evaluate effectiveness and identify additional opportunities for improvement. Promotes a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, employee engagement, and High Reliability Organization principles throughout the medical center. Provides education and mentorship related to performance improvement methodologies and organizational change. Coordinates oversight of facility SAIL performance measures and organizational quality metrics. Monitors national performance measures, analyzes trends, benchmarks organizational performance, and identifies opportunities for improvement. Collaborates with executive leadership, service chiefs, and program managers to develop, implement, monitor, and evaluate action plans to improve organizational performance. Prepares and presents executive reports, dashboards, scorecards, and performance analyses for the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), Quality Council, Governance Committees, and other organizational leadership groups. Provides consultation regarding interpretation of national performance measures, SAIL methodology, benchmarking, and strategic performance improvement initiatives. Coordinates facility responses to national performance reviews and collaborates with Quality Management, Accreditation, Patient Safety, Risk Management, Infection Prevention, and clinical services to support organizational excellence. Supports strategic planning activities through analysis of organizational performance data and continuous monitoring of quality outcomes. Promotes data-driven decision making and organizational accountability for sustained performance improvement. VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 am-4:30 pm Compressed/Flexible: May be Available Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
qualifications_text: Basic Requirements: English Language Proficiency. In accordance with 38 U.S.C. 7403(f), no person shall serve in direct patient care positions unless they are proficient in basic written and spoken English. Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE); OR Individuals attending a master's level bridge program in nursing who have completed coursework equivalent to a bachelor's level degree in Nursing may have opportunity to become registered as a nurse with a state licensing board prior to completion of the bridge program. Upon achievement of a State license, the individual may be appointed on temporary basis and later converted to a permanent appointment upon successful completion and graduation from the bridge program. (Reference VA Handbook 5005, Appendix G6); OR In cases of graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing, possession of a current, full, active, and unrestricted registration will meet the requirement for graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant an appointment as a Nurse who has completed an associated degree/entry level Nursing education program. Credit for foreign nursing education higher that associate degree/entry level requires a formal degree equivalency validation from a recognized equivalency evaluation accepted by VA such as International Consultants of Delaware (ICD). Current, full, active, and unrestricted registration as a graduate professional nurse in a State, Territory or Commonwealth (i.e., Puerto Rico) of the United States, or the District of Columbia. Graduate Nurse Technician (GNT) Exception: Candidates who otherwise meet the basic education requirements, but do not possess the required licensure, may be appointed at the entry step of the grade and level applicable to the completed nursing education as a GNT on a 120-day temporary appointment while actively pursuing licensure (may be extended up to two years on a case-by-case-basis.) NOTE: Grandfathering Provision - All persons currently employed in VHA in 0610 series and performing the duties as described in the qualification standard on the effective date of the standard (1/29/2024) are considered to have met all qualification requirements for the grade held including positive education and licensure/certification. Grade Determinations: The following Scope, Education and Dimension criteria must be met in determining the grade assignment of candidates, and if appropriate, the level within a grade. The Dimension requirements (Practice, Veteran/Patient Driven Care, Leadership, Professional Development and Evidence-Based Practice/Research) are detailed for each grade and level within the online assessment: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13056728. Grade/Level Scope Education Nurse I, Level I Delivers fundamental, knowledge-based care to assigned clients while developing technical competencies. An Associate Degree (ADN) or Diploma in Nursing, with no additional professional nursing required. Nurse I, Level II Demonstrates integration of biopsychosocial concepts, cognitive skills and technically competent practice in providing care to clients with basic or complex. An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 1 year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse I, Level 1 ;OR a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) with no additional professional nursing experience required. Nurse I, Level III Demonstrates proficiency in practice based on conscious and deliberate planning. Self-directed in goal setting for managing complex client situations. An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 2 years of professional nursing experience in which one year is equivalent to Nurse I, Level 2; OR a BSN and 1 year of professional nursing experience equivalent to the Nurse I, Level 2; OR a Master's degree in nursing (MSN) and no additional professional nursing experience; OR a Master's degree in a *related field with a BSN and no additional professional nursing experience. Nurse II Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others. A BSN with 2 years of professional nursing equivalent to Nurse I, Level 3; OR an MSN with one year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse I, Level 3; OR a Master's degree in a *related field with a BSN and one year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse I, Level 3; OR a Doctoral degree in Nursing with no professional nursing experience; OR a Doctoral degree in a *related field with a BSN with no additional professional nursing experience. Nurse III Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience and creative approaches to management of complex client care beyond the immediate practice setting. MSN and 2 years of specialized nursing experience, one of which is equivalent to Nurse II and meets all dimension requirements for Nurse III; OR a Master's degree in *related field with BSN and two years of specialized nursing experience, one of which is equivalent to Nurse II and meets all dimension requirements for Nurse III; OR a Doctoral degree in Nursing with and one year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse II and meets all dimension requirements for Nurse III; OR a Doctoral degree in a *related field with a BSN and one year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse II and meets all dimension requirements for Nurse III. *Note: Foreign education programs/degrees are not creditable as related degrees. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

title: Management and Program Analyst
job_summary: Protect your homeland and defend your culture. Join USCIS, America's frontline defense against illegal foreign infiltration and fraud. As a Management and Program Analyst, you will analyze data to support sound conclusions, recommendations, and decisions.
duties_text: The responsibilities described are for the full performance level. At developmental grade levels, assignments will be of more limited scope performed with less independence, and limited complexity. Communicate both orally and in writing to audiences of various sizes and from differing demographics; Support the implementation and coordination of a variety of initiatives impacting the E-Verify, and Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements(SAVE) Programs; Participate in various studies, working groups and testing of new business systems; Support the review of background information for studies, compiling statistical data from testing and evaluations; Support live events through exhibiting and/or public webinars.
qualifications_text: The qualifications for this position must be met by 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on 10/02/2026. Current Federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the lower grade or equivalent grade band in the Federal service. The Time-in-Grade requirement must be met by 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on 10/02/2026. Application Limit: This vacancy is limited to the first 150 applications received. All applications received prior to midnight 11:59 PM (ET) of the day the application limit is reached will be accepted and considered. If the application limit is not reached by the closing date of the announcement, all applications received during the open period will be considered. Any required documents must be submitted at the time that you apply as documents will not be accepted past the day the application limit is reached, if applicable. If you choose to edit your application after it has been submitted, it will be removed from consideration until you re-submit your application. The date your application is last submitted will be used to determine whether you meet the cut-off criteria. GS-05: You qualify at the GS-05 level if you possess three (3) years of general experience, one (1) year of which was equivalent to at least the GS-04 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Analyzing problems to identify significant factors, gathering pertinent data, and recognizing solutions; Planning and organizing work; Communicating effectively orally and in writing. OR You may substitute successful completion of a Bachelor's degree or a full 4-year course of study in any field leading to a Bachelor's degree for the experience required at the GS-05 grade level. This education must have been obtained from an accredited college or university. One year of full-time undergraduate study is defined as 30 semester or 45 quarter hours. GS-07: You qualify at the GS-07 level if you possess one (1) year of specialized experience, which is equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Performing statistical research to assist in the evaluation of management processes and functions; Examining documents and databases to support the development program objectives and improvements; Carrying out specified portions or segments of specific projects and/or studies; Compiling information for incorporation into final reports and/or briefings. OR You may substitute successful completion of one year of fulltime graduate education for the experience required at the GS-07 level. This education must have been obtained from an accredited college or university and demonstrate the skills necessary to do the work of the position. Check with your school to determine how many credit hours comprise a year of graduate education. If that information is not available, use 18 semester or 27 quarter hours. OR You may also substitute superior academic achievement for the experience required at the GS-07 level. You must have completed the requirements for a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with either: (1) class standing in the upper third of a graduating class or major subdivision; or, (2) a grade point average of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale based on four (4) years of education or the final two (2) years; or, (3) a grade point average of 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final two (2) years of the curriculum; or, (4) membership in a national scholastic honor society. GS-09: You qualify at the GS-09 level if you possess one (1) year of specialized experience, which is equivalent to at least the GS-07 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Performing analysis to resolve problems or improve effectiveness of operational or administrative programs; Representing the organization by providing information to internal and external stakeholders; Researching documents; compiling and charting statistical data; gathering, summarizing, and analyzing information; Carrying out specified portions or segments of specific projects associated with division programs and initiatives. OR You may substitute a Master's degree or two (2) full years of graduate education leading to such a degree in any field, or a J.D. or L.L.B. degree for experience required at the GS-09 grade level. Such education must have been obtained in an accredited college or university and demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of this position. Check with your school to determine how many credit hours comprise two years of graduate education. If that information is not available, use 36 semester or 54 quarter hours. Please read the following important information to ensure you submit everything we need to consider your application: It is your responsibility to ensure that you submit your responses and appropriate documentation prior to 10/02/2026. You must upload your resume under the "Resume" category. Resumes submitted under the "Other Documents" category will not be considered. Your most recently submitted resume will be used to determine your qualifications for the position advertised in this announcement. Therefore, your resume must highlight your most relevant, significant experience related to the requirements found in the qualification section of this announcement, as well as any applicable education. Limit your resume to no more than two pages. The USAJOBS database will not allow an applicant to submit an application that includes a resume over two pages. To help ensure your resume remains clear and easy to read, we recommend using margins of at least 0.8 inches and a font size of at least 11 point. Be clear and specific when describing your work history since Human Resources cannot make assumptions regarding your experience. Your application will be rated and ranked based on your responses to the online questions. Please ensure EACH work history includes ALL of the following information: Job Title (include series and grade if Federal Job) Duties (be specific in describing your duties) Employer's name and address Supervisor name and phone number Start and end dates including month, day and year (e.g. June 18 2007 to April 05 2008) Start and end dates for each grade/pay level if you've held a federal position. Full-time or part-time status (include hours worked per week) Salary Determining length of General or Specialized Experience is dependent on the above information and failure to provide the above information may result in a finding of ineligible. Protect your homeland and defend your culture. Join USCIS, America's frontline defense against illegal foreign infiltration and fraud. As a Management and Program Analyst, you will analyze data to support sound conclusions, recommendations, and decisions.
The responsibilities described are for the full performance level. At developmental grade levels, assignments will be of more limited scope performed with less independence, and limited complexity. Communicate both orally and in writing to audiences of various sizes and from differing demographics; Support the implementation and coordination of a variety of initiatives impacting the E-Verify, and Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements(SAVE) Programs; Participate in various studies, working groups and testing of new business systems; Support the review of background information for studies, compiling statistical data from testing and evaluations; Support live events through exhibiting and/or public webinars.

All applications received prior to midnight 11:59 PM (ET) of the day the application limit is reached will be accepted and considered. If the application limit is not reached by the closing date of the announcement, all applications received during the open period will be considered. Any required documents must be submitted at the time that you apply as documents will not be accepted past the day the application limit is reached, if applicable. GS-05: You qualify at the GS-05 level if you possess three (3) years of general experience, one (1) year of which was equivalent to at least the GS-04 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Analyzing problems to identify significant factors, gathering pertinent data, and recognizing solutions; Planning and organizing work; Communicating effectively orally and in writing. OR You may substitute successful completion of a Bachelor's degree or a full 4-year course of study in any field leading to a Bachelor's degree for the experience required at the GS-05 grade level. This education must have been obtained from an accredited college or university. One year of full-time undergraduate study is defined as 30 semester or 45 quarter hours. GS-07: You qualify at the GS-07 level if you possess one (1) year of specialized experience, which is equivalent to at least the GS-05 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Performing statistical research to assist in the evaluation of management processes and functions; Examining documents and databases to support the development program objectives and improvements; Carrying out specified portions or segments of specific projects and/or studies; Compiling information for incorporation into final reports and/or briefings. OR You may substitute successful completion of one year of fulltime graduate education for the experience required at the GS-07 level. This education must have been obtained from an accredited college or university and demonstrate the skills necessary to do the work of the position. Check with your school to determine how many credit hours comprise a year of graduate education. If that information is not available, use 18 semester or 27 quarter hours. OR You may also substitute superior academic achievement for the experience required at the GS-07 level. You must have completed the requirements for a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with either: (1) class standing in the upper third of a graduating class or major subdivision; or, (2) a grade point average of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale based on four (4) years of education or the final two (2) years; or, (3) a grade point average of 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final two (2) years of the curriculum; or, (4) membership in a national scholastic honor society. GS-09: You qualify at the GS-09 level if you possess one (1) year of specialized experience, which is equivalent to at least the GS-07 level in the federal government, that equipped you with the skills needed to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have experience performing the majority of the following duties: Performing analysis to resolve problems or improve effectiveness of operational or administrative programs; Representing the organization by providing information to internal and external stakeholders; Researching documents; compiling and charting statistical data; gathering, summarizing, and analyzing information; Carrying out specified portions or segments of specific projects associated with division programs and initiatives. OR You may substitute a Master's degree or two (2) full years of graduate education leading to such a degree in any field, or a J.D. or L.L.B. degree for experience required at the GS-09 grade level. Such education must have been obtained in an accredited college or university and demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of this position. Check with your school to determine how many credit hours comprise two years of graduate education. If that information is not available, use 36 semester or 54 quarter hours.
